title: Who's Who: Célestin Aubert
summary: Silver-film chemist whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Célestin Aubert (1794–1862) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a silver-film chemist whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.
Aubert prepared the films that made the 1829 reciprocal-impression experiments convincing. Marks appeared behind ordinary barriers, and controlled interruptions altered what returned.
He became famous for keeping his recipes secret, provoking a bitter dispute over whether private methods could support public science.

For Alderwick readers, Célestin Aubert is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
